summary: The statement and proof are correct. The global extension forces every lattice point of the convex hull into the positive support and makes the attained polyhedral convex roof agree with all prescribed heights, including boundary sites. The cube construction, vertical scaling, and thin complementary product give the asserted actual tables in the original integer dimension, including rank zero, and the curvature-cutoff comparisons yield the stated normalized convergence. The supplied accepted midpoint inequality applies to the auxiliary one-dimensional-base body; upper semicontinuity then extends dyadic log-concavity to all real coefficients, completing both directions of the equivalence and the transfer claims. The explicit four-site example verifies the failure of the weaker hypotheses for roof matching and realization. No mathematical errors or gaps were found, including in the zero-curvature, zero-height, boundary-fiber, and lower-rank cases.
